newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL tin rebounds on foreign demand, more gains seen.
newsitem.headline: KL tin rebounds on foreign demand, more gains seen.

text.p: Fresh foreign buying and a technical rebound in London helped Malaysian tin price rise to 13.85 ringgit ($5.51) a kg, after it fell to a 27-month low of 13.76 ringgit on Tuesday, traders said.
The metal rose nine cents from Tuesday's close.

"Yesterday's fall was too sharp. Prices are very cheap here and have attracted a lot of buying interest from Europe and Japan. Some Malaysian buyers also bought," a trader said, adding that he expected a further recovery.
"The metal is still undervalued and should attract more buying interest if London continues to rise tonight," he said.
The trader believed that the metal could firm back to the psychological level of 14 ringgit a kg by the end of the week.
The market saw an opening bid of 155 tonnes against offer of 109 tonnes. Final turnover was at 129 tonnes against 94 on Tuesday.
"Fundamentally, the market is still sound and physical demand is likely to be seen from Europe and Japan as KLTM prices are still competitive," the trader said.
The fall in London on Monday, mainly due to sales by fund managers, caused tin price here to fall to its lowest level in 27 months yesterday.
Despite a higher local premium over the London price, the market's near-term prospects look firm because of the strong growth in the regional tinplate and solder sectors, dealers said.
The local price premium over London widened to $75 a tonne against $55 on Tuesday.
